items.content:
RT @LiveOverflow: I took a closer look at the https://t.co/rtT8YaMOFZ CTF, which aims to demonstrate that PHP2SHELL is not realistically exploitable. So I gave it a try.

Note: My analysis could be wrong, and I'm more than happy to be proven otherwise.

Here’s what I found:
• The server responds with Server: nginx and X-Powered-By: PHP/8.4.26.
• My differential fingerprinting scanner independently confirmed at least PHP 8.2+
• Hypotheses: I considered two possible setups:
    ◦ nginx → PHP-FPM
    ◦ nginx → Apache → PHP-FPM/mod_php
• After comparing the server's behavior against local test environments, the closest match appears to be nginx → PHP cli-server.

Plot twist: the response behavior is consistent with the PHP cli-server serving a static index.html rather than an index.php. If that's indeed the case, the challenge appears to be intentionally made unexploitable.

My conclusion (for now) is that I'm questioning whether this is a good-faith challenge.

Happy to be corrected if I've missed something!

🚨 𝗣𝗛𝗣𝟮𝗦𝗵𝗲𝗹𝗹: 𝗰𝗼𝗻𝗻𝗲𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗵𝗼𝗻𝗲𝘆𝗽𝗼𝘁 𝘁𝗲𝗹𝗲𝗺𝗲𝘁𝗿𝘆 𝘄𝗶𝘁𝗵 𝗲𝗻𝗱𝗽𝗼𝗶𝗻𝘁 𝗽𝗿𝗲𝘃𝗮𝗹𝗲𝗻𝗰𝗲
​
An interesting correlation while looking at the ongoing PHP2Shell activity.
​
The 𝗗𝗲𝗹𝗳𝘁 𝗧𝗵𝗿𝗲𝗮𝘁 𝗜𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗹𝗹𝗶𝗴𝗲𝗻𝗰𝗲 𝗟𝗮𝗯, running 𝟯𝟬𝟬 𝗵𝗼𝗻𝗲𝘆𝗽𝗼𝘁𝘀, has been capturing real-world PHP2Shell activity, including attempts to move beyond scanning into OS command execution, PHP code delivery, and malware deployment.

https://t.co/AzsAQRu8PM
​
One of the associated malware samples has the SHA256:
​
𝟶𝚌𝟻𝟺𝟾𝟼𝚏𝟶𝟼𝟼𝟸𝟶𝚎𝟸𝟼𝚎𝟹𝟷𝟼𝚏𝟺𝚋𝟹𝟹𝚏𝟹𝟷𝟾𝚋𝟶𝚍𝟼𝟺𝟼𝚍𝟻𝚎𝟷𝟷𝟹𝟹𝟽𝟾𝟿𝟹𝟹𝟷𝚊𝚊𝟸𝚏𝚎𝚍𝟶𝟷𝟸𝟹𝟼𝟶𝚍𝟷𝟺𝟾𝟼
​
Looking at the same SHA256 in 𝗠𝗶𝗰𝗿𝗼𝘀𝗼𝗳𝘁 𝗗𝗲𝗳𝗲𝗻𝗱𝗲𝗿, the file prevalence shows 𝟲 𝗱𝗲𝘃𝗶𝗰𝗲𝘀 𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗹𝗱𝘄𝗶𝗱𝗲, with: 🔹 First seen: 𝟮𝟮 𝗢𝗰𝘁 𝟮𝟬𝟮𝟲, 𝟭𝟭:𝟱𝟲 𝗔𝗠 🔹 Last seen: 𝟮𝟯 𝗢𝗰𝘁 𝟮𝟬𝟮𝟲, 𝟴:𝟬𝟭 𝗔𝗠
​
What makes this interesting is the timing. The Defender observations closely follow the new attack telemetry recorded by the honeypot infrastructure.
​
This doesn't prove that those 6 devices were compromised through PHP2Shell, but it demonstrates the value of 𝗰𝗼𝗿𝗿𝗲𝗹𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗳𝗿𝗲𝘀𝗵 𝗵𝗼𝗻𝗲𝘆𝗽𝗼𝘁 𝗶𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗹𝗹𝗶𝗴𝗲𝗻𝗰𝗲 𝘄𝗶𝘁𝗵 𝗲𝗻𝗱𝗽𝗼𝗶𝗻𝘁 𝘁𝗲𝗹𝗲𝗺𝗲𝘁𝗿𝘆 to understand how quickly newly observed threats may surface across environments.
​
𝗛𝗼𝗻𝗲𝘆𝗽𝗼𝘁 → 𝗜𝗢𝗖 → 𝗘𝗻𝗱𝗽𝗼𝗶𝗻𝘁 𝘁𝗲𝗹𝗲𝗺𝗲𝘁𝗿𝘆 → 𝗧𝗵𝗿𝗲𝗮𝘁 𝗵𝘂𝗻𝘁
